chose: Detect undeclared redundancy as ENUMERATED-DOMAIN AGREEMENT: collect every site that spells out a set of string tokens (union members, enum members, object/Record keys, switch cases, ===-comparison chains, string-literal arrays, markdown table first columns, a|b|c alternations inside string literals), then pair sites whose token sets overlap
over: Signature-shaped twin detection: two functions with the same parameter and return types
Clone detection over normalized token streams (the classic copy-paste detector)
Duplicate magic-literal detection (the same rare number written in two places)
because: The declared parity form is agreement over an ENUMERATED DOMAIN, so the undeclared version of it must be a domain spelled twice. Type-shape twins are hopelessly common in TS ((s:string)=>string appears everywhere) and clone detection finds copy-paste, which is a maintenance smell, not a divergence risk -- neither is informative WITHOUT a prior claim about the value, which is the whole point. A duplicated token SET is: if the two sets are unequal the transcription has already drifted, which is signal with no declaration needed.

chose: Suppress a candidate pair when the TYPE SYSTEM already ties the two sites together (Record<Union,V>, Omit<Config,...>, a shared type link) and report the suppression count out loud
over: Reporting every duplicated key set and letting the reader filter
Suppressing on a name-similarity heuristic instead of the type link
because: A Record<OracleVerdict,X> table CANNOT drift from its union -- tsc checks the keys. Reporting it is a false positive by construction, and this repo's own ladder says that tier belongs to the type system, not to coherence. On the first dogfood run 15 of 35 overlapping pairs were compiler-enforced: without this rule the report would have been ~40 percent noise before any ranking. It also gives the reader the tier-1 FIX for free -- annotate the literal and the finding disappears.

chose: Exclude test files from site collection entirely
over: Scanning tests too, since a hand-copied domain in a test is real redundancy
because: A hand-enumerated domain inside an oracle is ALREADY a finding -- oracle-domain.ts's meta-oracle fails a via-test boundary whose loop iterates a literal. A second detector reporting the same thing in a different voice is duplicated tooling, which is the exact defect class this command exists to name.

chose: Ship a hard reporting floor (score >= 3.5) plus --all, and report precision from a dogfood run rather than claiming it
over: No floor: print all 35 overlapping pairs ranked
A --check mode that gates CI on new candidates
because: The brief's constraint was five true pairs over fifty candidates. Unfloored output on this repo is 35 pairs of which roughly 5 matter; the tail is dominated by union-vs-comparison-chain pairs where a code path legitimately reads part of a domain. Gating is worse than useless here: the detector has no way to know an intended difference from a drifted one, so a gate would train people to suppress it.

chose: A derivable-bound arm: checking a computed statistic against a bound the tool could derive (4,237 removed lines attributed to a 1,139-line file)
because: That is a RUNTIME consistency check over numbers a tool produced, not a static property of source text. It needs an instrumented producer that declares its own bounds (a diff stat cannot exceed the file's line count) -- a different mechanism from anything in this module, closer to a contract on a computation than to duplicate-domain detection. Building a weak static approximation would have made the command mean two unrelated things. Named here so the next agent does not assume 'redundancy' already covers it.

chose: Ship the CHAIN_METHODS/ITER_METHODS false positive rather than add a rule that hides it
over: A rule suppressing two same-file adjacent list literals where one is a strict superset
because: That rule fits exactly one pair in one repo. The superset relation is genuinely the redundancy shape -- what makes this instance benign is domain knowledge (the two lists mean different things) that no static rule has access to. Tuning it away would overfit the detector to its own dogfood corpus and would silently start hiding real supersets elsewhere. Reported as a false positive in the precision number instead: 4 of 5 true at the default floor.
